description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of chicken are simmered in a mildly spiced, velvety gravy, offering a truly comforting and indulgent experience. This iconic dish is perfect for a satisfying lunch or a special family dinner.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, and 1/2 tsp salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, or even overnight for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another tablespoon of butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onion and cook until translucent and soft, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and sugar. Add salt to taste. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil separates. Add 1/2 cup water or chicken stock if the sauce becomes too thick.

instructions.title: Blend and Finish the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the pan from heat and let it cool slightly. Using an immersion blender, or carefully transferring to a regular blender, blend the sauce until it is smooth. Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low heat. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed Kasuri Methi. Mix until well combined and heated through, but do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces back into the creamy sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Let it simmer for another 2-3 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

tips: For a truly smooth sauce, after blending, pass the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any remaining solids. This gives it a restaurant-quality texture.
Adjust the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder to control the spice level; it primarily provides color. For more heat, add a pinch of regular red chili powder.
Always add the heavy cream at the very end and avoid boiling the sauce afterwards to prevent it from curdling and to maintain its rich, velvety texture.
article:
Mastering the Art of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Indian Lunch Guide

There are few dishes that evoke as much comfort and delight as a perfectly made Butter Chicken. Known globally by its Hindi name, Murgh Makhani, this iconic Indian curry has captivated palates with its rich, creamy texture, tantalizing aroma, and a symphony of balanced flavors. Far more than just a meal, it’s an experience – a culinary journey that takes you straight to the heart of India’s vibrant cuisine. Whether you’re a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore new flavors, creating authentic Butter Chicken from scratch is a rewarding endeavor. Perfect for a hearty Indian lunch or a special dinner, this dish promises to be a crowd-pleaser every time. Get ready to embark on a flavorful adventure as we guide you through everything you need to know to make the best Butter Chicken you've ever tasted.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

At its heart, Butter Chicken (or Murgh Makhani, meaning "chicken with butter") is a classic Indian curry featuring tender pieces of chicken, traditionally cooked in a tandoor (clay oven), enveloped in a velvety smooth, spiced tomato and butter sauce. Originating in Delhi in the 1950s, it quickly became a staple, beloved for its mild yet deeply flavorful profile. The magic of Murgh Makhani lies in its delicate balance: the sweetness of tomatoes and a touch of sugar or honey, the tanginess of yogurt and lemon, the warmth of aromatic spices like garam masala and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and the undeniable richness imparted by butter and cream. While it offers a complex depth of flavor, it’s remarkably approachable, making it a favorite for those new to Indian cuisine and a comforting classic for connoisseurs. Its signature orange hue and luxurious texture make it instantly recognizable and irresistibly appealing as a centerpiece for any Indian lunch.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

Preparing authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key components, each playing a crucial role in building the dish's signature flavor profile. Don't be intimidated by the list; many ingredients are pantry staples, and the reward is truly worth it.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Creamy Tomato Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   2 green cardamom pods
*   1 cinnamon stick (1-inch piece)
*   2 bay leaves
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup cashews, soaked in hot water for 15-20 minutes
*   1/2 cup water (or chicken broth)
*   1 teaspoon sugar or honey (to balance acidity)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1/4 cup heavy cream
*   1 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   Fresh coriander leaves, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Murgh Makhani

Creating this beloved Murgh Makhani at home is a process of layering flavors. Follow these steps for a truly memorable experience:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients (yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice). Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, until lightly charred and cooked through. The slight charring adds a wonderful smoky depth, mimicking the tandoor. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the whole spices (cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, bay leaves) and sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic.

4.  **Build the Tomato Gravy:** Lower the heat and add the powdered spices (red chili powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric). Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to prevent burning. Immediately add the crushed tomatoes and the soaked, blended cashews (blend cashews with a little water until smooth). Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer. Add ½ cup of water or broth, sugar/honey, and salt. Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken.

5.  **Achieve Silky Smoothness:** Carefully remove the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaves). Allow the sauce to cool slightly, then transfer it to a blender. Blend until perfectly smooth. For an extra luxurious texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step removes any tiny bits of onion or spice, resulting in the signature silky Murgh Makhani gravy.

6.  **Finish the Curry:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low-medium heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces and simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors. Stir in the heavy cream and the crushed kasuri methi. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, ensuring the sauce doesn't boil rapidly after adding cream. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The rich, creamy goodness of Butter Chicken is now ready!

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

While the recipe provides a solid foundation, a few expert tips can elevate your Butter Chicken from good to absolutely legendary:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken soaks in the yogurt and spices, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination is highly recommended.
*   **Charred Chicken for Depth:** The slight char on the chicken pieces is crucial. It adds a smoky, tandoor-like flavor that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani. If you have a grill, using it for the chicken can enhance this effect further.
*   **The Power of Blending and Straining:** For that restaurant-quality, velvety smooth sauce, don't skip blending and straining. It makes a significant difference in texture.
*   **Toast Your Kasuri Methi:** Lightly dry-roast the kasuri methi in a dry pan for a few seconds until fragrant before crushing it between your palms and adding it to the curry. This awakens its essential oils, intensifying its unique aroma and flavor.
*   **Balance is Everything:** Butter Chicken is all about balance. Taste the sauce before the final simmer and adjust the sugar (for sweetness), lemon juice (for tang), and salt as needed. A perfectly balanced sauce is the hallmark of a great Murgh Makhani.
*   **Good Quality Ingredients:** Use fresh, good-quality spices, ripe tomatoes, and full-fat dairy for the best results.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

The rich, creamy goodness of Butter Chicken deserves equally delightful accompaniments. It's truly a versatile dish that pairs well with a variety of Indian breads and rice dishes, making it an ideal Indian lunch.

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, fluffy naan (especially garlic naan or butter naan) is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the luscious sauce.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps soak up the flavors.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** These whole wheat Indian flatbreads are also excellent choices for a more rustic feel.
*   **Garnish:** Always finish with a generous sprinkle of fresh coriander leaves for freshness and color. A dollop of extra cream or a small knob of butter on top before serving adds to the presentation and richness.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) or a cooling raita (yogurt dip) can provide a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.

## Variations and Substitutions for Murgh Makhani

While the classic Butter Chicken is perfect as is, you can easily adapt this recipe to suit different dietary needs or preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cheese) for Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu, chickpeas, or a mix of vegetables like potatoes and peas.
*   **Vegan Version:** Substitute dairy yogurt with a plant-based alternative (like coconut or almond yogurt) for marination. Use coconut cream instead of heavy cream, and coconut oil or a vegan butter substitute instead of butter. Ensure all spices are vegan.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. To maintain thickness, you can add a tablespoon of poppy seeds (soaked and ground) or a very small cooked potato, blended into the sauce.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For less heat, use only Kashmiri chili powder for color. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Use lean chicken breast, low-fat yogurt, and reduce the amount of butter and cream. You can also increase the vegetable content by adding pureed carrots or bell peppers to the sauce.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a recipe; it's a culinary journey that rewards you with incredible flavors and aromas. By following these detailed instructions and tips, you're well on your way to creating a truly unforgettable Butter Chicken experience right in your own kitchen. Enjoy this beloved Indian lunch classic with family and friends!
